transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-28
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Victor (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Raj (Cascade), Emily (Cascade), Tom (Cascade procurement)

Summary (auto): quick check-in to align on renewal timeline, discuss capacity upgrade for upcoming Q4 product push, and adding EU region for data residency. Customer asks about cost delta for dedicated pool + eu region. Redwood to run benchmark and send formal quote.

00:00 Sophie: hey everyone thanks for joining, um I'll kick off — this is our renewal and expansion check-in for Cascade systems. quick agenda: renewal timing, capacity needs, region add, security follow-ups.
00:18 Raj: yeah thanks Sophie, appreciate it. first off high-level — our Q4 release will push search+summarization to 40k users so we need dedicated capacity; right now the hosted plan is hitting limits.
00:34 Victor: got it, when you say hitting limits, is that steady qps or spike related?
00:40 Raj: mostly spikes, like end of day batch and customer events; latency spikes to 600—700ms on p99 which is too high.
00:46 Emily: and we also have stricter residency needs for EU customers so we'd like a frankfurt region, can't put that data through the US deployed hosts.
00:54 Sophie: understood, capacity + region. for renewal you were looking at a 12-month extension? Tom — is that correct from procurement side?
01:02 Tom: yes, 12 months preferable. also want predictable unit pricing and an SLA tie-in. if we move to dedicated, we need a clear uptime and latency SLO.
01:12 Lena: for the SLA we can provide an SLA for Dedicated with monthly credits for breaches. we'll include latency SLOs based on your selected config.
01:20 Raj: what about cost — rough delta versus hosted? we did a quick calc but it's fuzzy.
01:26 Sophie: ballpark: dedicated reserved pools typically reduce per-token cost by ~25—35% versus bursty hosted for sustained throughput; adding EU region is an add-on — we'll put exact numbers in the quote.
01:36 Raj: ok — can you also confirm if KMS integration is supported, and audit logs for compliance? that's a must.
01:42 Victor: yes KMS/HSM via customer-managed keys is supported on Private and Dedicated — hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood KMS but we can do customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private. audit logs and per-request tracing are available in the Console.
01:56 Emily: perfect. can you provide the SOC2/ISO docs and the network architecture for VPC peering?
02:02 Sophie: we'll share the compliance pack after the call, and Victor can attach a network diagram.
02:08 Victor: I'll include sample VPC setup and notes on firewall rules; also we'll note recommended autoscale thresholds to avoid latency spikes.
02:16 Raj: on benchmarks — we want a short run on our workload characteristics. we'll send a sample prompt set and expected seq lengths.
02:24 Sophie: great — can you send that by monday?
02:26 Emily: yes we'll send the payload distribution and peak qps by end of day tomorrow.
02:32 Victor: once we have that Victor will run a two-hour perf test on a dedicated pool similar to your config and share p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
02:42 Raj: and how long to spin up an EU dedicated pool if we greenlight it?
02:48 Lena: for dedicated pools, lead time is typically 7—10 days for provisioning in a new region, faster if there's existing capacity. we'll mark burst options for initial ramp.
02:56 Tom: procurement question — can we add an amendment to our existing contract rather than a full new MSA?
03:02 Sophie: yes that's the standard path — we can do a contract amendment for term extension and region/capacity add. Lena will prepare the amendment.
03:08 Tom: also escalation path — we need named contacts and 24/7 for Sev1s.
03:14 Lena: we'll include escalation contacts and an SLA appendix for Sev1 response times.
03:20 Raj: any risk of model parity — if you route to cheaper variants for fallback, will behavior change for our models?
03:27 Victor: good question — we have compatible model variants and we can pin a specific version for production to guarantee behavior, and fallback policies can be configured to prefer quality-preserving fallbacks. we'll document the tradeoffs.
03:36 Raj: ok nice. competitor question — we're also evaluating in-house serving and VertexAI on price but they don't have the same operational tooling.
03:44 Sophie: understood — we'll include a unit economics sheet in the quote to compare.
03:50 Emily: timeline — we need the updated quote asap, if renewal decision by 6/10 we can align provisioning for Q3 ramp.
03:58 Sophie: action list then: Victor runs perf benchmarks; Sophie sends quote; Lena drafts amendment; Cascade sends workload profile. anyone else?
04:06 Tom: that's it from procurement. thanks.
04:09 Sophie: thanks all, we'll follow up by end of week with artifacts.

Post-call notes (auto): transcription has a few mis-hearings (proper nouns slightly off), but content aligns with typical renewal/expansion playbook.
